article.story: BLACKSBURG, Va. -- — Ben Hammond and Amani Hansberry totaled 15 points apiece, and Jaylen Curry scored 14 to lead Virginia Tech to an 85-68 victory over Richmond on Monday night. Hammond shot 6 for 15 with two 3-pointers and seven assists for the Hokies (5-0). Hansberry made 4 of 8 shots, sinking a 3-pointer and all six of his free throws, while Curry made 4 of 11 shots and went 6 for 6 at the foul line. Tyler Johnson added a double-double off the bench for Virginia Tech with 10 points and 11 rebounds. Jamie Kaiser Jr. finished with 17 points and six rebounds to pace the Spiders (3-2). Dominick Stewart added 13 points, and Amon Dorries scored 11. Curry had six points, and Virginia Tech never trailed in a game-opening 20-9 run. Efrem Johnson made two straight 3-pointers to increase the Hokies' lead to 35-19, and the advantage grew to 20 before Collin Tanner made a layup in the final seconds to cut it to 41-23 at the break. Kaiser hit a 3-pointer and scored five, and Derin Saran's three-point play finished off a 15-0 run to start the second half as Richmond closed within 41-37. Miles Heide tipped in a miss to end the run, and Hammond scored seven in a 14-4 spurt that left the Hokies leading 55-41 with 13:22 remaining. The Spiders got no closer than eight from there. Up next Richmond plays Western Kentucky on Friday at the Greenbrier Tip-Off. Virginia Tech plays Northwestern on Friday at the Charleston Classic. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full men’s basketball coverage here
